lesson.text: Quick memory: in grade 5 you met how living things reproduce. Do all living things make new living things like themselves? Yes: it is one sign of life.
All living things are made of cells, the smallest units of life. Some living things are a single cell; you are made of trillions.
Most cells are too small to see without a microscope. Robert Hooke first saw cells in cork in 1665 and named them after small rooms.

Parts of a cell: the cell membrane controls what goes in and out; the nucleus holds the instructions (DNA) and runs the cell; the cytoplasm is the jelly where the work happens; mitochondria release energy from food.
Plant cells also have a cell wall, which makes them stiff, and chloroplasts, where photosynthesis happens.
Try it in the world: build a giant plant cell from blocks in your world: glass for the membrane, a stone wall round it, green blocks for chloroplasts and a big nucleus. Next: body systems.

exercises.prompt: What is the smallest unit of life?
exercises.hint: Every living thing is made of them.
exercises.explain: Cells are the smallest units of life.

exercises.prompt: All living things are made of cells.
exercises.hint: Think of plants, animals and you. What are they all made of?
exercises.explain: Yes: every living thing is made of one or more cells.

exercises.prompt: Which part of a cell holds its instructions (DNA)?
exercises.hint: The control centre.
exercises.explain: The nucleus holds the DNA and runs the cell.

exercises.prompt: What do you need to see most cells?
exercises.hint: micro means small.
exercises.explain: A microscope makes tiny things look bigger.

exercises.prompt: A bacterium is a living thing made of just one cell.
exercises.hint: Some living things are a single cell.
exercises.explain: Yes: bacteria are single cells.

exercises.prompt: Which part controls what goes in and out of a cell?
exercises.hint: It is like a gate around the cell.
exercises.explain: The cell membrane lets some things in and keeps others out.

exercises.prompt: Which part releases energy from food?
exercises.hint: The cell's power stations.
exercises.explain: Mitochondria release the energy in food.

exercises.prompt: Which parts do plant cells have but animal cells don't?
exercises.hint: What makes plants stiff and green?
exercises.explain: Plant cells have a stiff cell wall and chloroplasts.

exercises.prompt: Chloroplasts are where photosynthesis happens.
exercises.hint: Plants make food from sunlight in them.
exercises.explain: Yes: chloroplasts use sunlight to make food.

exercises.prompt: What is cytoplasm?
exercises.hint: It fills the cell.
choices: the jelly where the cell's work happens
exercises.explain: Cytoplasm is the jelly inside the cell where its work happens.

exercises.prompt: Why is a plant stem stiff even without bones?
exercises.hint: What do plant cells have that animal cells don't?
choices: Its cells have stiff cell walls.
exercises.explain: Stiff cell walls hold the plant up.

exercises.prompt: A cell is found with chloroplasts. What does this tell you?
exercises.hint: Which cells have chloroplasts?
choices: It is probably from a plant.
exercises.explain: Chloroplasts are found in plant cells.

exercises.prompt: Animal cells have a cell wall.
exercises.hint: Only one kind has a wall.
exercises.explain: No: animal cells have a membrane but no cell wall.

exercises.prompt: Order from smallest to largest.
exercises.hint: Cells build everything else.
exercises.explain: Cells make tissues, tissues make organs, organs make an organism.

exercises.prompt: Why did Robert Hooke call them cells?
exercises.hint: A cell can mean a small room.
exercises.explain: In cork they looked like rows of small rooms.

exercises.prompt: Match each cell part to its job.
matches: controls what goes in and out
exercises.hint: Think of a school: the head's office, the gate, the power station, the kitchen.
exercises.explain: The nucleus holds the DNA; the membrane controls what goes in and out; mitochondria release energy; chloroplasts make food from light.

exercises.prompt: Sort the cell parts: in both plant and animal cells, or only in plant cells?
exercises.hint: Which parts make plants stiff and green?
exercises.explain: The nucleus, membrane and cytoplasm are in both. The cell wall and chloroplasts are only in plant cells.

exercises.prompt: Sort the living things: a single cell, or many cells?
exercises.hint: Is it a tiny living thing you need a microscope to see, or something big?
exercises.explain: A bacterium and an amoeba are each just one cell. An oak tree, a person and a mushroom are made of many cells working together.

exercises.prompt: A cell is like a factory. Match each part to its factory job.
exercises.hint: Think about each part's job: runs the cell, lets things in and out, releases energy, or where work happens.
exercises.explain: The nucleus runs the cell, like a manager's office. The membrane controls what goes in and out, like a gate with guards. Mitochondria release energy, like a power station. The cytoplasm is where the work happens: the factory floor.

exercises.prompt: A scientist sees a cell under a microscope. Sort the clues: it must be a plant cell, or it could be either?
items: it has a stiff cell wall
exercises.hint: Which parts do only plant cells have?
exercises.explain: Chloroplasts and a stiff cell wall show it is a plant cell. A nucleus, a membrane and mitochondria are in plant and animal cells alike, so they can't tell you which.
